title: Design Ops
descriptionHtml:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.


⚡ The design and research community at Alan

Alan’s Design & Research (D&R) community is the group of designers and researchers behind everything our members see and use. Our goal is simple: build the most member-centric health experience there is, with high standards of craft and a real understanding of the people we design for.

We are growing fast, and AI is changing what is possible in the way we work. We are looking for someone who loves tooling, ops and AI to help us move faster without lowering the bar on quality.

This is a builder role where design, operations and AI meet. You will scope where AI and automation can help us build faster, scale better and catch quality issues earlier, then turn the best ideas into tools the community actually uses. Along the way, you will help us improve our rituals and best practices, and share what we learn inside and outside Alan. You are not a designer or a researcher yourself: you are the enabler that allows the community to go faster and perform better as our member base grows.

🤝 Your missions

You will help D&R work smarter and keep quality high as we grow, in close collaboration with the community, its lead, and the engineering, Product Ops and platform teams we work with. You will help shape our community strategy on AI and tooling, then build and run what comes out of it.

  • Explore: Test new AI tools and automations, find the ones that really save time or improve quality, and share the best with the community. Work with our internal AI tooling teams to bring what’s cutting edge to design and research.

  • Build: Create skills, agents and automated checks that make design and research work more efficient, reliable and of higher quality.

  • Run the tooling: Maintain and upgrade the tools the community relies on, and be our point of contact with Alan’s platform and agentic teams.

  • Improve how we work: Bring in better practices and rituals, push our existing rituals to the next level and help us show what we learn and achieve, inside and outside Alan.

  • Own your roadmap: Identify opportunities, prioritize solutions, set clear goals, track adoption and quality, and adjust as you go.

🚀 You are a good fit if...

You are an ops-minded builder with around 4 years of experience in ops or enablement roles: design ops, tooling, automation, analytics, program management or something close. Design and research interests you, but what drives you is helping teams work better with tools, automation and better rituals.

What you bring

  • Hands-on experience automating work. You have replaced repetitive tasks with automations, internal tools or AI workflows (no-code, low-code or AI tools), at work or on your own projects, and you can tell us what you built and who used it.

  • Familiarity with AI tools. You have built or tested skills, agents or automations, and you care that they are reliable, not just impressive in a demo.

  • Comfort working with engineers. You can build things yourself, you know when to ask for production-grade work, and you speak their language.

  • Experience supporting a team or community, for example through onboarding, rituals, events or internal communications.

  • Strong English communication, to collaborate with our international team. French is a plus.

Nice to have

  • Experience in or alongside a design or research team.

  • Familiarity with Figma and design systems.

Qualities we look for

  • Builder and strategic mindset: you make progress with incomplete information, choose the simplest approach that works, and ship.

  • Rigour: you set a baseline and a target, and improve with each iteration.

  • Systems thinking: you see how people, processes, tools and data fit together.

  • Judgment: you frame ambiguous problems, prioritise, and know what to drop.

  • Clear communication: you keep people updated and explain your choices.

title: Diesel Mechanic
descriptionHtml:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

We are currently seeking a skilled Diesel Mechanic to join our team. The successful candidate will be responsible for maintaining, repairing, and troubleshooting diesel engines and related systems on our autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) to ensure optimal performance and reliability.

 

Responsibilities

  • Diagnose and repair diesel engine malfunctions, mechanical issues, and electrical faults using diagnostic tools, technical manuals, and troubleshooting techniques.

  • Inspect and test diesel engine components, systems, and subsystems to identify and address potential problems or areas of concern.

  • Overhaul and rebuild diesel engines and associated systems, including fuel injection systems, turbochargers, and exhaust systems, as needed to restore performance and efficiency.

  • Maintain accurate records of maintenance and repair activities, including parts used, labour hours, and service performed, to track equipment history and ensure compliance with maintenance schedules and regulatory requirements.

  • Follow safety protocols and procedures for working with diesel engines and related equipment, including proper handling and disposal of hazardous materials and fluids.

  • Collaborate with other maintenance technicians, engineers, and operators to troubleshoot complex problems, share technical knowledge, and implement effective solutions.

 

Qualifications

  • Marine Diesel and/or Volvo VODIA experience required

  • GCSEs (or equivalent) are required. A recognised vocational qualification or apprenticeship in diesel mechanics, marine engineering, or a related discipline is preferred.

  • Proven experience as a diesel technician or a diesel mechanic, with demonstrated proficiency in diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining diesel engines and related systems.

  • Strong mechanical aptitude and technical skills, with the ability to read and interpret technical manuals, diagrams, and schematics.

  • Familiarity with diagnostic tools and equipment used in diesel engine repair, such as scan tools, multimeters, and oscilloscopes.

  • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot complex mechanical and electrical issues.

  • Effective communication skills and the ability to work independently or as part of a team.

  • Willingness to work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment with changing priorities and deadlines.

  • Ability to travel as needed to meet business objectives, including throughout the Indo-Pacific region and to our headquarters in Austin, Texas. This role will require spending 30+ days training at Saronic headquarters in Austin, Texas.

 

Physical Demands

  • Ability to perform physically demanding work for extended periods.

  • Du entwickelst mit Produkt, Analytics und Media Operations unsere Angebote weiter und bringst zurück, was Agenturen wirklich brauchen

    ... und du pflegst deine Pipeline und deinen Forecast so, dass wir uns darauf gemeinsam verlassen können

Dein Profil


Hinweis: Niemand erfüllt alle Anforderungen zu 100 %. Wenn du dich stark mit der Rolle identifiziert und Lust auf richtig guten Mediavertrieb hast, freuen wir uns trotzdem auf deine Bewerbung. Denn wir wollen gemeinsam mit dir wachsen.

  • Du bringst mehrere Jahre Erfahrung im digitalen Mediavertrieb mit, zum Beispiel bei einem Vermarkter, Publisher, einer Plattform oder auf Agenturseite

  • Du kennst die deutsche Agenturlandschaft und hast idealerweise ein belastbares Netzwerk in den Agenturen

  • Du hast digitale Kampagnen selbst aufgesetzt und ausgesteuert, idealerweise in DV360 (YouTube) und im Meta Ads Manager, und sprichst über CPM, Reichweite und Conversion so sicher wie über Markenziele

  • Du arbeitest gern mit Daten und kannst aus Zahlen eine Geschichte machen, die ein Kunde versteht und kauft

  • Du präsentierst komplexe Sachverhalte zielgruppengerecht und überzeugend, vor der Planer:in genauso wie vor der Marketingleitung

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert und zuverlässig, auch wenn mehrere Angebote und Buchungen gleichzeitig laufen

  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau sowie verhandlungssicheres Englisch

    Benzin im Blut ist kein Muss, Neugier auf die Automobilbranche schon.

Und was springt für dich dabei raus?

Bei uns findest du ein innovatives, vielfältiges und lockeres Arbeitsumfeld im Herzen Münchens. Dazu kommen:

Vielfalt und Inklusion sind fest in unserer Unternehmenskultur verankert. Wir freuen uns über jede Bewerbung und treffen unsere Entscheidungen fair, transparent und ausschließlich auf Basis von Fähigkeiten, Erfahrung und Potenzial.

title: Director, Data Strategy, UK (FTC)
descriptionHtml:
About WPP Media

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. With exceptional talent, trusted data and intelligence, and world-class partnerships – all united by our pioneering agentic marketing platform, WPP Open – we help clients navigate change, capture opportunity, and deliver transformational growth. 

WPP Media is WPP's AI-driven media operating unit, bringing together media, data, and partnerships to deliver creative personalisation at scale. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.

For more information, visit wppmedia.com.

3363 - Director, Data Strategy, UK (FTC) 

Role Summary and Impact 

We are seeking a Director to join our Data Strategy team for our major UK telco client, BTEE.
The BTEE team (aka OpenConnect) is one of the largest UK client in the agency and the data work on the account is innovative and future-facing, with clients who are data savvy and champion our work across their business.
This role is focused on the Consumer side of the BT Group business and will work across three of BT Group’s sub-brands; BT, EE and Plusnet.

Data Strategy involves transforming the way our clients think about, organize and orchestrate data & technology to deliver more timely, engaging and meaningful brand experience for their customers. 

BT Consumer is a data rich client and that combined with clients willingness to test and evolve makes for opportunities to do agency leading work. Work is recognised by awards, agency-first’s and also TelCo-firsts for the EMEA market. This role will be part of an agency-team-wide-push to adopt AI and drive innovation to drive client outcomes.

The main focus area of this role are as below;


Data-led audience and bidding strategy enablement;

  • Using the data-sets and technology available to BTEE, lead and oversee the delivery of test, trial and strategy recommendations across paid media campaigns on addressable channels.
  • Working closely with the Transformation lead and ensuring broader strategic workstreams and acceleration projects find a place in campaign activity and are set up in a way that's measurable and methodical.

Technology Project Ownership;

  • As part of the BTEE’s Media Acceleration Roadmap, you will own broader workstreams to drive outcomes across DPAM use-cases, including the clients roadmap with Amazon Marketing Cloud.
  • You will be part of wider workstreams that bring together the power of WPP as a group, which for example could include working with parts of the business beyond WPP Media, in order to bring new exciting projects to BT.

Cross-functional Collaboration;

  • You will be in charge of Open Connect’s paid media Audience Approach and Audience Playbook, ensuring this stays up to date. 
  • Maintaining and improving Data Strategy ways of working in the campaign cycle with other internal agency practices on the BT account.
  • Be a conduit between technical and less technical teams within the agency, ensuring alignment on project goals and client objectives and speaking in the correct data language to the clients.
  • Work with the client and embedded agency teams to define, justify and request future signals and data products which can drive the clients business goals. This includes our internal Tech & AI Consulting team and the embedded engineering team at BTEE who build data products for us.

Leadership

  • This role sits in the Operations Pod of the team, alongside a Data Strategy Associate Director, Data Strategy Manager and a Data Strategy Associate.
  • Each team member will own the Data Strategy for a specific product vertical but you will lead this Pod. You will need to ensure they are producing high quality work and look to unblock any challenges they have.

Skills and Experience

  • Deep interest in Media & Technology: An understanding of and desire to learn more about data products, AI, technology, and trends within the advertising and marketing industry with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Customer Focus: A relentless focus on client success, with a passion for delivering exceptional client experiences and driving long-term relationships.
  • Communication and Presentation Skills: Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills, as this role hinges on effective interaction with clients and agency partners.
  • Experience managing multiple stakeholders in a matrixed environment
  • 6+ years digital agency-side working on a data-led role either agency, vendor or client side, with a strong emphasis on digital paid media.
  • Highly developed interpersonal, team building and relationship management skills
  • TelCo experience preferable but not required
  • Understanding of the importance of privacy first media and what that means for how we need to do things differently

Life at WPP Media & Benefits

Our passion for shaping the next era of media is powered by our commitment to Be Extraordinary, investing in our employees to inspire transformational creativity. We also Lead Optimistically, firmly believing in and Championing Growth and Development for every individual. This commitment allows WPP Media employees to leverage the extensive global WPP Media & WPP networks to pursue their passions, build vital professional connections, and learn at the cutting edge of marketing and advertising. 

We Create an Open environment built on trust and respect, where everyone feels they belong and has opportunities to progress. This inclusive culture is fostered through a variety of employee resource groups and frequent in-office events showcasing team wins, sharing thought leadership, and celebrating holidays and milestone events. Our comprehensive benefits package reflects this commitment, including competitive medical, group retirement plans, vision, and dental insurance, significant paid time off, preferential partner discounts, and employee mental health awareness days. 

WPP Media is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to characteristics. We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection in this open and supportive environment. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.  Please note that while our philosophy is the same across WPP, benefits may vary by office/country.

Please note this is a UK based role and requires individuals to have the right to work in this location

Please read our Privacy Notice (https://www.wppmedia.com/pages/privacy-policy) for more information on how we process the information you provide.

While we appreciate all applications received, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Director of Human Resources
descriptionHtml:
At CesiumAstro, we are developers and pioneers of out-of-the-box communication systems for satellites, UAVs, launch vehicles, and other space and airborne platforms. We take pride in our dynamic and cross-functional work environment, which allows us to learn, develop, and engage across our organization. If you are looking for hands-on, interactive, and autonomous work, CesiumAstro is the place for you. We are actively seeking passionate, collaborative, energetic, and forward-thinking individuals to join our team.

We are looking to add a Director of Human Resources to our team in Munich, Germany. Reporting to the Vice President of Human Resources, this role will lead HR management and service delivery for employees and leaders across Germany, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom, partnering with local stakeholders and global HR colleagues as the business grows.

This is a hands-on, multi-country HR leadership role for a builder and operator. As the company expands its engineering, operational, and manufacturing capabilities, you will strengthen HR practices across the three countries, support organizational growth, and help managers and employees navigate change.

This position combines regional HR leadership with practical execution. You will partner with the Vice President of Human Resources and leaders across engineering, manufacturing, operations, programs, and corporate functions, staying close to day-to-day needs while implementing people initiatives across our European operations.

The successful candidate will bring strong HR generalist and business-partnering experience in a technically complex environment, a sound understanding of German employment practices, and the ability to manage effective, locally appropriate HR delivery in Switzerland and the United Kingdom. You will balance business priorities, employee experience, compliance, and hands-on delivery without unnecessary bureaucracy.


JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead and develop HR colleagues and coordinate local HR support and service partners across Germany, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom, establishing clear service expectations, accountability, and responsive support for employees and managers.
  • Oversee country-level HR operations, including onboarding, offboarding, employment documentation, payroll and benefits coordination, and local service provider relationships.
  • Implement and improve HR processes, policies, documentation, and workflows that support workforce growth, operational efficiency, and consistent service delivery while accommodating country-specific requirements.
  • Serve as a trusted HR partner to business leaders across Germany, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom, providing guidance on workforce planning, organization design, performance management, employee relations, and organizational change.
  • Develop a strong understanding of CesiumAstro's technology, products, programs, customers, and operating priorities while collaborating with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Program Management, Supply Chain, Finance, and other functions to address workforce and organizational challenges.
  • Translate business plans and growth objectives into coordinated HR priorities, headcount plans, organizational structures, hiring requirements, and workforce initiatives in partnership with Finance, Talent Acquisition, and business leaders.
  • Implement consistent approaches to performance management, talent reviews, career development, succession planning, and internal mobility while adapting company frameworks to local employment requirements.
  • Coach managers on employee development, leadership effectiveness, performance conversations, organizational structures, decision rights, and accountability.
  • Identify talent gaps, employee concerns, leadership challenges, and workforce risks while recommending practical actions that strengthen employee engagement, retention, and organizational effectiveness.
  • Manage employee relations concerns, performance issues, grievances, workplace investigations, and sensitive employee matters, coordinating with Legal and local specialists to support fair, consistent, and timely resolution.
  • Partner with global HR, Legal, Finance, country leadership, and local advisers to align HR policies and practices with employment laws, employee representation or consultation requirements, and data protection obligations across Germany, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
  • Support organizational changes and leadership transitions across the three countries, coordinating with global HR, Legal, and employee representatives or consultation bodies where applicable.
  • Maintain accurate HR data across Germany, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom, using workforce metrics and people analytics to identify trends, evaluate workforce risks, and inform management decisions.
  • Support workforce requirements across technical and operational teams, including staffing plans, onboarding, employee engagement, retention, and workforce scheduling.
  • Promote CesiumAstro's culture of speed, ownership, technical excellence, and collaboration while strengthening HR service quality, operational consistency, and organizational effectiveness across Europe.

    • JOB REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Law, or a related field with 11–15 years of related experience, or Master's degree in a related field with 9–12 years of related experience in human resources management, HR business partnering, employee relations, workforce planning, organizational development, or a related human resources discipline.
  • 5+ years of progressive leadership or management experience leading human resources initiatives, developing HR professionals and managers, or overseeing HR operations and business partnering activities.
  • Experience supporting engineering, manufacturing, aerospace, hardware technology, or another technically complex organization.
  • Experience improving HR programs or processes in a growing organization; experience in a scale-up environment is an advantage.
  • Practical experience in employee relations, performance management, workforce planning, talent development, and organizational change.
  • Ability to deliver consistent HR processes across borders while working with in-country HR partners, payroll or benefits providers, and specialist employment advisers.
  • Experience supporting employees and managers in Germany and managing or coordinating HR activities across more than one European country; experience with Switzerland and/or the United Kingdom is an advantage.
  • Good working knowledge of German employment law and HR practices, including works council processes where applicable, together with familiarity with the distinct employment, employee consultation, and data protection requirements of Switzerland and the United Kingdom and an ability to engage local experts.
  • Ability to manage sensitive employee relations matters across different legal and cultural environments with discretion, fairness, and sound judgment.
  • Ability to improve HR processes and implement consistent, workable solutions without unnecessary complexity.
  • Business acumen and the ability to connect people decisions with operating needs, staffing plans, and organizational performance.
  • Comfort using HR systems, workforce data, and people metrics to support decisions and track results.
  • Ability to work effectively in a growing, fast-paced environment with changing priorities and evolving structures.
  • Ability to influence, constructively challenge, and coach managers and senior functional leaders.
  • Professional fluency in German and English, with clear written and verbal communication skills across international teams.
  • Ability and willingness to work on-site in Munich and travel as needed to company locations in Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
  • Hands-on and execution-oriented leadership style with a strong ownership mentality and attention to detail.
  • Familiarity with export-controlled or otherwise regulated environments is beneficial.

title: Director of International Product
descriptionHtml:
About Lyra
Lyra Health is the leading provider of mental health solutions for employers supporting more than 20 million people globally. The company has delivered 13 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 20 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness and cost efficiency. Extensive peer-reviewed research confirms Lyra’s transformative care model helps people recover twice as fast and results in a 26% annual reduction in overall healthcare claims costs. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions.

Lyra is looking for a visionary and strategic Director, International Product to lead and scale our global mental health offerings. As Lyra grows around the world, you’ll shape how we deliver high-quality, culturally relevant care to members, providers, and employers in every market we serve.

You’ll serve as the connective tissue between our global commercial ambitions and technical execution, guiding multiple simultaneous initiatives and building a platform-first, repeatable engine for international growth. Working alongside senior leadership, you’ll own the strategic vision, delivery, and performance of the international product suite.

The leaders who thrive in this role pair high standards with real care for the people around them. They build strong relationships across the organization, earn influence through trust and clarity, and bring steady, energizing leadership to their teams, especially when the path ahead is uncertain


What You'll Do:
  • Global Product Vision & Strategy: Define the multi-year vision and roadmap for Lyra’s international product suite, grounded in market analysis, competitive insight, and firsthand understanding of the members, providers, and clients we serve in each region. Synthesize global market signals into a clear point of view on where to invest for the greatest impact for global employers.
  • Product Scope & Ownership: Hold full lifecycle responsibility for the scoping, development, and delivery of member experiences and the underlying platform infrastructure across four major product lines: International Lyra Workforce Mental Health (WFMH), Global Lyra Wellbeing, 10 Local Lyra Wellbeing products, and other product surface areas as needed.
  • Platform-First Scale: Lead the evolution of our international offerings onto a unified global platform, with automated workflows that make each new client launch faster and more repeatable than the last. Champion the localization of core capabilities, including billing, eligibility, and provider management, so they flex gracefully across markets.
  • Roadmap Stewardship: Balance the needs of today’s clients with durable, long-term platform investments. Make clear, well-reasoned tradeoffs, explain the “why” behind them in a way that brings people along, and have the conviction to say “not yet” when that’s what best serves members and the business.
  • Leadership & Team Development: Build and lead the International Product team. Hire and grow exceptional people, including leaders whose strengths go beyond your own, and invest in their development through candid, caring feedback and meaningful ownership. Your success is measured by how well your team thrives: clearing the path, providing context, and creating the conditions for others to do their best work.
  • Business Ownership & Resourcing: Create and manage the annual budget for International Product. Assess resourcing needs and build compelling business cases to secure the investment needed to reach ambitious growth targets.
  • Cost-to-Serve & Performance Insight: Partner with the Data organization to build a single, trusted view of international performance, giving leadership clear visibility into margins, ROI, and utilization. Define and track the product metrics that measure success, and identify opportunities to streamline and automate so global products are built for long-term profitability.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Serve as the central connector across Product, Engineering, Data, Operations, Clinical Governance, Legal, and Compliance. Build trusted relationships across regions and time zones, including in our local operations work toward win-win outcomes amid competing priorities, and ensure clinical quality and local regulatory requirements are built into the product lifecycle from the start.
  • Go-To-Market Partnership: Act as a trusted partner to Go-To-Market and Client Services teams. Serve as the product voice in high-stakes, C-level client conversations and complex RFPs, bringing the technical and clinical confidence that helps Lyra win and retain large-scale global contracts.
  • AI-Enabled Product Excellence: Maintain a high bar for product craft and apply AI with purpose, both in our products, where it can meaningfully expand access and improve care, and in how we work. Model how AI can accelerate research, synthesis, planning, and execution, and help your team adopt tools and practices that drive efficiency, effectiveness, and happiness.

    • What You'll Bring:
  • Experience: Several years in product management, strategy, or technical operations.
  • Leadership: Several years of people leadership, with a track record of building strong teams and coaching talent to grow beyond their current roles.
  • Global Product Expertise: Experience launching and scaling products across multiple countries, including localizing for language, culture, and care norms, and navigating regional privacy and regulatory frameworks (e.g., GDPR, data residency). A natural instinct to design for local context, informed by real cultural fluency.
  • Platform & Enterprise Architecture: Deep understanding of bringing multiple systems together onto a unified global platform and reducing the effort required for each new client launch.

title: Director of Software Engineering
descriptionHtml:
The Role:

Spire is making a fundamental shift in how it operates its constellation. We are moving from a model where trained operators watch dashboards and escalate to experts, to one where the system is fully autonomous, self-healing, and data intelligent. This Director will lead that transformation. You will set the technical vision, define the architecture, build and inspire the team, and personally raise the standard for what modern space operations look like.

The old model relies on operators, escalations, manual processes, and institutional knowledge locked in the heads of a few experts. It does not scale and it does not belong in a modern space company. We know what we want to replace it with: SRE principles applied to a constellation, autonomous fault handling, AI-driven anomaly detection, low toil, high data quality, and continuous improvement baked into the system.


What This Role Is Not:

This is not a role for someone who wants to graduate out of technical work. If your ideal week is back-to-back 1:1s, sprint ceremonies, and stakeholder syncs, this is not the right fit. We need a director who writes code, reviews architecture, challenges technical decisions, and earns the team's respect through demonstrated craft and not just tenure or title.


What You Will Work On:


Technical Leadership

  • Define and own the technical roadmap for autonomous constellation operations
  • Set the architectural direction for the data platform, reliability systems, and automation infrastructure
  • Stay hands-on: review code, prototype solutions, and get into the details when it matters
  • Establish engineering standards across code quality, system design, testing, and observability, and hold the team to them
  • Be the person engineers come to when the problem is genuinely hard

Team Building & Culture

  • Recruit, develop, and retain a team of 6 to 10 world-class reliability and platform engineers
  • Set the pace, tone, and ambition for the team and make being on it feel like a privilege
  • Create an environment where engineers grow fast, own their work, and ship things they are proud of
  • Identify gaps and level up engineers through mentorship and not just management

Operational Transformation

  • Lead the shift from manual, operator-driven processes to fully automated and self-healing operations
  • Define and drive toward SLOs, error budgets, and reliability targets for the constellation
  • Partner with satellite operations and mission teams to translate pain into software solutions

Cross-Functional Influence

  • Be the technical voice of the team in company-wide conversations about architecture, infrastructure, and platform strategy
  • Influence how Spire thinks about automation, data, and AI/ML across the broader engineering organization

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 3 in a technical leadership or staff-level individual contributor role
  • Demonstrated track record building and shipping reliable production systems at scale. You have owned things that could not go down.
  • Deep technical credibility. Engineers on your teams have respected your judgment and not just your title.
  • Experience with SRE principles, reliability engineering, or large-scale automation. You have reduced toil systematically and not just complained about it.
  • Strong foundation in Python, distributed systems, data platforms, and cloud infrastructure
  • Experience hiring and developing engineers. You know what great looks like and how to find it.
  • The communication and influence skills to drive technical decisions across teams you do not directly control

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience applying AI/ML or advanced analytics to operational or monitoring problems
  • Experience writing performance software in Rust
  • Background in space systems, aerospace, or highly constrained real-time environments
  • Experience building data lakes, telemetry platforms, or observability infrastructure at scale
  • A history of leading teams through technical transformations and not just maintaining the status quo

Spire operates a hybrid work model, and this position will require you to work a minimum of three days per week in the office.

descriptionHtml:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Location: United Kingdom
Role Type: Individual Contributor
Initial Scope: UK, with the potential to expand across the Commonwealth over time
Travel: Significant UK travel with some international travel as required

Your Impact

Axon is looking for a strategic seller to help build our Defence, National Security, Public Safety and Critical Infrastructure business in the UK.

This is not intended to be a traditional product overlay or specialist advisory role. We are looking for someone who can build a market, create pipeline, develop strategic relationships and establish the partner ecosystem required to scale.

The role will focus across Defence, National Security, Public Safety, Critical National Infrastructure, airports, ports, defence supply chain and other strategically important infrastructure.

The right person will bring a combination of Defence / National Security experience, commercial sales experience and a strong understanding of how to build and leverage channels, primes, systems integrators and strategic partners.

Initially this will be a UK-focused individual contributor role. As the business and opportunity mature, there is potential for the remit to expand more broadly across the Commonwealth.

What You’ll Accomplish

In the First 6 Months

  • Build a clear UK market strategy across Defence, National Security, Public Safety and Critical Infrastructure.
  • Identify and prioritize the highest-value target accounts, programs and routes to market.
  • Establish relationships with key Defence, government, public safety, national security and critical infrastructure stakeholders.
  • Build a focused network of primes, systems integrators, resellers and strategic partners who can extend Axon’s reach.
  • Develop a qualified pipeline with clear customer problems, buying paths, partners and next steps.
  • Create greater awareness of Axon’s capabilities beyond individual products and position the broader ecosystem against customer outcomes.

In the First 12 Months

  • Build a meaningful and repeatable pipeline across the segment.
  • Close initial strategic opportunities and establish referenceable customers and partners.
  • Establish several high-value channel relationships that create scalable access to Defence, Public Safety and Critical Infrastructure opportunities.
  • Position Axon as a credible participant in major Defence, public safety, national security and critical infrastructure programs.
  • Create a repeatable GTM model that can eventually be expanded into Canada, Australia, New Zealand and the broader Commonwealth.

What You’ll Do

Build the Market

Own the commercial strategy for the UK Defence, National Security, Public Safety and Critical Infrastructure segment.

Identify where Axon can create differentiated value across airspace awareness, drone detection, real-time operations, situational awareness and the broader Axon ecosystem.

Develop the market rather than wait for traditional inbound opportunities or formal tenders.

Sell Strategically

Own a defined set of strategic accounts and opportunities.

Develop relationships at senior levels across Defence, government, public safety, national security and critical infrastructure organizations.

Understand complex customer problems, procurement processes, funding paths and decision structures and translate them into executable commercial strategies.

This role should be comfortable operating through long and complex sales cycles while maintaining clear commercial accountability.

Build the Channel

Develop strong relationships with primes, systems integrators, resellers, consulting partners and other organizations already operating within the Defence, public safety and security ecosystem.

Determine where Axon should lead an opportunity directly and where we are better positioned as a technology partner, subcontractor or component of a broader solution.

Build scalable routes to market rather than trying to pursue every opportunity directly.

Connect the Axon Ecosystem

Look beyond a single product or capability.

Identify opportunities where Dedrone, DFR, Fusus, real-time operations and other Axon capabilities can contribute to a broader customer outcome.

Work closely with Product, SE, CSM and regional sales teams to bring the right capabilities into each opportunity.

Influence Across the Organization

Operate effectively in a matrixed global organization.

This person will need to influence Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, Professional Services and executive leadership without relying on formal authority.

They should be comfortable identifying gaps, creating clarity and driving action across teams.

What You Bring

We are looking for someone who has demonstrated success in environments similar to the one we are trying to build.

The strongest candidates will likely have:

  • Meaningful experience within Defence, National Security, Public Safety or a closely related environment.
  • Commercial experience selling complex technology or solutions into Defence, government, public safety or critical infrastructure.
  • Experience building and managing channel relationships, including primes, systems integrators, resellers and strategic partners.
  • A strong understanding of government and Defence procurement and how large programs move from concept to funding and execution.
  • Credibility with senior military, government, law enforcement, security and critical infrastructure stakeholders.
  • Experience creating pipeline and opening new markets rather than simply managing an established territory.
  • Strong commercial instincts and demonstrated ability to close complex opportunities.
  • Comfort operating as a hands-on individual contributor.
  • The ability to influence across functions and organizations without formal authority.
  • Strong judgment, resilience and a high degree of ownership.

title: Director Service Accounts (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
Director Service Accounts @ Sereact 🦾

Director Service Accounts (m/f/d) · Stuttgart, with frequent travel to customer sites across Europe · Reports to the VP Operations · Full-time

Who we are

Sereact builds the robot brain for physical work. Cortex, our vision-language-action foundation model, is hardware-agnostic: the same model runs single-arm and dual-arm systems and mobile manipulators that pick, sort and handle returns in live production across Europe and the US. Customers include Zalando, IKEA, BMW, Rohlik and DHL.

Founded in 2021 in Stuttgart, with an R&D hub in Zurich and a US office in Boston. We have raised more than $145 million, most recently a Series B led by Headline, with Zalando as a strategic investor. We work in small, senior teams with a flat structure; execution counts more than titles.

Why this role, why now

The Site Acceptance Test is where a deployment ends and a customer’s operation begins. From that day our robots pick in someone else’s building, every shift, against targets the customer measures. Many of our customers buy Sereact as a service: they pay for robots that work, not for robots that were delivered.

Our deployments are growing from single robots to fleets, and the site that performs is the site that grows. We now want one leader who owns every live site from SAT on: keeps it at target, brings it everything we ship in software and hardware, speaks for the customer inside Sereact, and turns a working site into a growing one.

The Real-World Learning Loop runs through your sites

Cortex learns from live deployments. Every station at a customer is part of that loop, so a station that is down is more than a service problem: a cell sitting dark is a stopped sensor.

  • In-Situ Policy Execution. Every live station runs the current policy in a real operation. Your surface on it: each site at target, every shift.

  • Continuous Data Acquisition. Robots annotate their own work while they run. Your surface on it: stations that run and stay connected, so the data keeps coming.

  • Data Curation and Learning. Failures and edge cases decide what Cortex learns next. Your surface on it: what your sites tell us reaches engineering and research with the context they need.

  • Evaluation and Policy Redeployment. Updated policies pass validation gates before they return to the fleet. Your surface on it: they land in your customers’ operations on a schedule the customer can plan around, with a way back if something is off.

A site that runs well teaches Cortex more, and it grows.

Responsibilities

  • Take over every site at SAT. Set the standard for what a site needs before your team takes it on: documentation, open points, spare parts, contacts and targets. If a site is not ready, it stays with deployment until it is.

  • Keep every site at target. Own each site’s performance against its contract: availability, throughput and pick success. See a problem coming before the customer does, and run the recovery plan when a site falls behind.

  • Run planned change. Software releases and model updates reach customer operations in a rhythm customers can plan around: release notes, change windows, blackout periods, validation on site and a rollback path.

  • Run hardware updates and retrofits across the installed base, from new gripper generations to station upgrades and fixes, with Hardware Engineering and the field teams, without stopping the customer’s operation.

  • Get every site ready for peak: hypercare and coverage plans for the weeks that matter most to our customers, from Black Friday to the January returns wave.

  • Be the customer’s advocate inside Sereact. Bring their priorities into product, R&D, hardware and operations, make sure what we promised at SAT holds, and own the customer communication when something goes wrong.

  • Take each site from SAT to expansion with Strategic Accounts: the performance evidence, the site capacity and the technical plan for the next stations. Strategic Accounts own the contract; you make the expansion ready to happen.

  • Report site health customers trust: one view of every site, monthly performance reports and the operational part of every business review.

  • Build and lead the Service Accounts team: Service Account Managers who each own a portfolio of live sites, and a playbook that still works when the installed base is ten times larger.

  • Work hand in hand with Deployment, Technical Support & Field Service, Hardware Engineering, R&D and Strategic Accounts, so a live site gets one coordinated answer, not five.

Not in scope, by design

  • Deployment up to SAT stays with our deployment teams. You set the bar for what you take over.

  • Incidents, the support desk, field technicians and spare parts logistics stay with Technical Support & Field Service. You own the site; they own the ticket.

  • Contracts, pricing and the expansion deal itself stay with Strategic Accounts. You make the case; they sign it.

  • Product and hardware design stay with engineering. You bring them what the field needs.

What makes this role hard

  • Every change to a live operation is a risk, and not changing is a risk too: the fleet only gets better if updates reach it. You make both safe.

  • Our robots work in other people’s buildings: their WMS, their conveyors, their shift patterns, their peak. Much of what decides a site’s performance is not ours, and it is still your problem.

  • You sit between the customer and our teams. Sometimes the customer’s priority is not ours. You argue for it, or you explain honestly why not.

  • The installed base grows faster than any team. What works by heroics today breaks at ten times the size.

Your first 12 months

  • First 90 days: know every live site and its people; one named owner, one health view and a clear status against target for each; a handover standard at SAT agreed with deployment.

  • By month 6: releases and retrofits in a rhythm customers can plan around; peak season run on hypercare plans; account plans with Strategic Accounts for the largest customers; the first Service Account Managers hired.

  • By month 12: every site at target or on a dated recovery plan; expansions coming out of the installed base; a playbook ready to take to the US.

What you bring

  • 8+ years owning live installations of complex automation after go-live (warehouse automation, intralogistics, robotics or comparable 24/7 systems), as service account manager, technical account manager, customer success or service delivery lead, including at least three years leading a team.

  • You did it while the installed base grew from tens to hundreds of sites, and you built the processes rather than inheriting them.

  • Technical enough to read a log, follow a root cause and hold your own with engineers. Commercial enough to sit with a customer’s operations director and talk performance, cost and growth.

  • You have run releases, upgrades and retrofit programs in live operations without stopping them.

  • Customers trust you because you tell them early and you tell them straight.

  • Fluent English and German; another European language is a plus.

  • You are happy to spend a large part of your week at customer sites.

Nice to have: subscription or Robotics-as-a-Service models · goods-to-person and AS/RS integrations · e-commerce, returns or grocery fulfilment · experience in both a scale-up and an established automation vendor.

Not the right fit: account management without technical depth, or running a ticket queue without ever owning a customer.

Three questions we will ask you

  1. Tell us about a live site that fell behind its targets. What did you change in the first two weeks, and how did it end?

  2. A customer’s peak starts in four weeks. Engineering wants to ship a model update and a gripper retrofit before then. What do you do?

  3. How do you know a site is about to grow, or about to leave, before the customer tells you?

What we offer

  • A fleet in live production that grows every month, and the mandate to build the team that keeps it at target.

  • A key role in the operations leadership of a company scaling from Europe into the US, with equity.

  • Travel, accommodation and meals covered when you are on site.

  • Our HQ in Stuttgart, with teams in Zurich and Boston.

How we hire

Conversations with our VP Operations and the founders, a working session on a real case from one of our live sites, and time with the team in Stuttgart. We move fast.

title: Embedded Software Engineer (NWB)
descriptionHtml:
For over four decades, Cirrus Logic has been propelled by the top engineers in mixed-signal processing. Our rockstar team thrives on solving complex challenges with innovative end-user solutions for the world's top consumer brands. Cirrus Logic is also known for its award-winning culture, built on a foundation of inclusion and fairness, meaningful community engagement, and delivering enjoyable employee experiences at every turn. But we couldn’t do it without our extraordinary workforce – and that’s where you come in. Join our team and help us continue to make Cirrus Logic an exceptional place to grow your career!
We’re looking for an Embedded Software Engineer who thrives close to the hardware and enjoys building high-performance, reliable firmware for DSP architecture and microcontrollers (e.g., RISC V and Arm Cortex M/A). You’ll design and implement real-time embedded software, optimize compute-heavy pipelines, and collaborate with hardware and systems teams to bring products from concept to production. This role suits someone who can move comfortably between architecture/design, low-level firmware, and performance tuning—especially where latency, throughput, power, and determinism matter.
Key Responsibilities:
  • Design, implement, and maintain embedded firmware for DSP cores and MCUs (RISC V and/or Arm).
  • Build and optimize real-time signal-processing pipelines (fixed-point and/or floating-point), potentially including FFTs, filters, modulation/demodulation, codecs, feature extraction, or control loops.
  • Develop firmware using a mix of C/C++ (and selective assembly where appropriate), with strong focus on performance, memory, and power optimization.
  • Work with SoC/board peripherals: DMA, timers, SPI, I²C, UART, I²S/TDM, PWM, GPIO, and relevant bus fabrics.
  • Bring up new hardware: boot flows, clocks, memory maps, interrupt vectors, peripheral init, and early validation.
  • Implement and debug drivers and RTOS components (e.g., Zephyr or equivalent), including task scheduling, synchronization primitives, and ISR design.
  • Develop test strategies: unit tests, hardware-in-the-loop tests, test automation, and manufacturing/production diagnostics.
  • Use debugging/profiling tools: JTAG/SWD, logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, trace (ETM/ITM), and cycle-accurate profiling when available.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with hardware, FPGA/ASIC, systems, and application teams to define requirements and interfaces.
  • Contribute documentation: architecture notes, interface specs, timing budgets, work packages, and bring-up guides.
  • Participate in code reviews and help establish best practices for embedded quality, safety, and maintainability.

    • Required Skills and Qualifications:
  • Strong professional experience developing embedded firmware in C/C++ for MCUs and/or DSPs.
  • Hands-on experience with RISC V and/or Arm architecture (Cortex M/A), including interrupts, memory, caches, and performance characteristics.
  • Solid understanding of embedded software fundamentals:
  • register-level programming, memory-mapped I/O
  • concurrency (ISRs, RTOS tasks), race conditions, timing determinism
  • fixed-point arithmetic, numerical precision, and overflow/underflow management
  • Proven ability to optimize firmware: cycle counting, memory layout, DMA usage, cache behavior, minimizing latency and jitter.
  • Comfortable with toolchains and build systems:
  • GCC/LLVM-based toolchains, cross-compilation
  • CMake/Make, Meson, linker scripts, map files
  • Strong debugging skills with hardware and firmware:
  • JTAG/SWD debugging
  • root-cause analysis of timing and performance issues
  • Source control expertise (Git) and disciplined engineering practices (code reviews, CI).

    • Preferred Skills and Qualifications:
  • Languages: C, C++, (optional) assembly, Python for test tooling/scripts
  • Architectures: RISC V, Arm Cortex M/A, DSP cores
  • RTOS/OS: Zephyr, embedded Linux (optional)
  • Tools: JTAG/SWD debuggers, GDB, OpenOCD/J-Link, logic analyzer, oscilloscope, trace tools
  • Practices: profiling, timing analysis, unit/integration testing, CI/CD for embedded
  • Experience with common DSP libraries/techniques (e.g., CMSIS-DSP, vendor DSP libs) and SIMD/vector optimization patterns.
  • Experience with Zephyr, or embedded Linux on Arm.
  • Familiarity with bootloaders, secure boot, OTA update mechanisms, and field diagnostics.
  • Understanding of digital communications, or audio, processing domains.
  • Exposure to safety/security standards (e.g., MISRA C/C++, IEC 61508, ISO 26262)

title: Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:

Van medische apparatuur en industriële systemen tot geavanceerde semicon-oplossingen: onze Electrical Engineers staan aan de basis van technologie die wereldwijd wordt toegepast. Ben jij de leider die energie krijgt van het ontwikkelen van mensen, kennis en technische excellence? Dan maken we graag kennis met je!

Als Electrical Engineering Manager beweeg jij je op het snijvlak van technologie, leiderschap en organisatieontwikkeling. Daarbij richt je je niet alleen op de resultaten van vandaag, maar ook op de technische uitdagingen van morgen. Je stimuleert kennisontwikkeling, versterkt engineering excellence en helpt richting te geven aan de verdere groei van Electrical Engineering binnen Benchmark.

Je geeft leiding aan een team van circa 40 engineers en speel je een belangrijke rol in de verdere ontwikkeling van een van de grootste technische disciplines binnen Benchmark. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de kwaliteit, groei en prestaties van de organisatie en creëert een omgeving waarin engineers kunnen excelleren, innoveren en zich blijven ontwikkelen.

Met jouw visie op leiderschap, talentontwikkeling en technologie bouw je aan een sterke engineeringcultuur waarin vakmanschap, samenwerking en continue verbetering centraal staan. Zo zorg je ervoor dat onze Electrical Engineering-organisatie klaar blijft voor de complexe technologische vraagstukken van onze klanten én de ambities van de toekomst.

Jij combineert technisch leiderschap, people management en strategische ontwikkeling. Daarom ben jij verantwoordelijk voor:

  • Het aansturen, coachen en ontwikkelen van circa 40 Electrical Engineers.

  • Het leiden van de AI-transformatie binnen Electrical Engineering.

  • Het neerzetten van een duidelijke visie op Electrical Engineering en het vertalen hiervan naar de praktijk.

  • Het stimuleren van innovatie, kennisontwikkeling en technische excellentie binnen het vakgebied.

  • Het ontwikkelen van competenties, groeipaden en vakmanschap binnen jouw team.

  • Het bewaken van de kwaliteit, capaciteit en inzetbaarheid van de afdeling.

  • Het ondersteunen en adviseren van Program Managers bij complexe ontwikkelprojecten.

  • Het aantrekken, selecteren en ontwikkelen van technisch talent.

  • Het versterken van de samenwerking met internationale engineering teams binnen Benchmark.

  • Het bijdragen aan organisatie brede besluitvorming als onderdeel van het Competence Management Team en aan een lerende organisatie waarin kennisdeling, ontwikkeling en continue verbetering centraal staan.

Samen met de managers van Software Engineering, Mechanical Engineering en Test Development Engineering werk je aan de verdere ontwikkeling van de totale engineeringorganisatie. Daarnaast werk je nauw samen met collega’s uit andere disciplines, waaronder HR. Omdat het aantrekken en ontwikkelen van talent in deze schaarse arbeidsmarkt essentieel is, beschik je over een sterk professioneel netwerk en weet je talent aan je team en organisatie te verbinden.

Waarom deze functie?

Deze rol biedt de unieke kans om invloed uit te oefenen op zowel de technische richting als de ontwikkeling van een grote groep professionals. Je werkt in een omgeving waar complexe technologie, internationale samenwerking en persoonlijke groei samenkomen.

Wat biedt Benchmark?

Bij Benchmark werk je aan producten die ertoe doen! Daarnaast zijn wij bij uitstek een organisatie waar je vrijheid krijgt, waar ondernemerschap wordt beloond en waarin je de ruimte krijgt om je ideeën tot uitvoering te brengen. We bieden je een dynamische omgeving met de ruimte om snel stappen te maken, door te groeien en verantwoordelijkheid te nemen. Je bent onderdeel van een wereldwijd bedrijf waar de nuchtere Twentse cultuur bewaard is gebleven.

Bij ons krijg je uitdagend werk, veel vertrouwen en ruimte om jezelf te blijven ontwikkelen. Je werkt met nuchtere collega’s in een informele cultuur, met goede voorwaarden om duurzaam te presteren.

Daarnaast bieden wij:

  • Een aantrekkelijk salaris passend bij de verantwoordelijkheden en het potentieel binnen de rol.

  • Een bonusregeling gekoppeld aan de prestaties van jouw team en de organisatie.

  • Een managementcontract met veel ruimte voor ondernemerschap, eigen verantwoordelijkheid en impact op de verdere ontwikkeling van de organisatie.

  • Persoonlijke groei en ontwikkeling, waarbij we samen een ontwikkelpad creëren dat aansluit op jouw ambities en de behoeften van de organisatie.

  • Flexibiliteit in de inrichting van je werkweek, met ruimte om werk en privé op een manier te combineren die voor jou werkt.

  • Een sterk kennisgedreven engineeringklimaat, waarin samenwerking, kennisdeling en innovatie centraal staan. Via initiatieven zoals Lunch & Learn-sessies en Pitch Discovery Sessions krijg je volop ruimte om te leren, te inspireren en nieuwe ideeën te ontwikkelen.

Wie ben jij?

Of je nu een ervaren engineering manager bent of toe bent aan je eerste grotere leiderschapsrol, jij krijgt energie van technologie én het ontwikkelen van mensen. Je weet professionals te verbinden, richting te geven en samen resultaten te behalen in een complexe high-tech omgeving. Met jouw technische achtergrond, nieuwsgierigheid en leiderschapspotentieel bouw je mee aan de volgende generatie engineers én innovaties. Je combineert flexibiliteit met een sterke interesse in technologie, bent van nature nieuwsgierig en floreert in een agile omgeving. Herken jij jezelf hierin? Dan maken we graag kennis met je.

Daarnaast zien wij graag:

  • Een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding in embedded software, elektrotechniek, natuurkunde of een vergelijkbare technische richting.

  • Je hebt een stevige achtergrond in electrical engineering en voldoende technische diepgang om met engineers en architecten te sparren over technische keuzes en ontwikkelrichtingen.

  • Minimaal zeven jaar ervaring binnen een hightech-ontwikkelomgeving, inclusief enkele jaren in een leidinggevende rol of een technische leiderschapsrol.

  • Aantoonbare ervaring met het aansturen, coachen en ontwikkelen van engineeringteams binnen een complexe technische organisatie.

  • Het vermogen om technische visie, organisatiedoelstellingen en talentontwikkeling succesvol met elkaar te verbinden.

  • Uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden en een goede beheersing van zowel de Nederlandse als Engelse taal.

Serious Tech
Bij Benchmark werk je voor bedrijven die impact maken met hun innovaties. Zo ontwikkelen we nieuwe producten die de veiligheid of gezondheid verbeteren of juist het gemak vergroten. Deze producten worden geleverd vanaf het productontwerp tot en met volumeproductie en soms ook rechtstreeks aan de eindgebruiker. Dit gehele proces wordt geheel in Almelo uitgevoerd, waar we samenwerken met ongeveer 650 collega’s

We werken aan innovaties voor, onder andere, semicon, gezondheidszorg, aerospace en industrie. Van productontwerp tot volumeproductie: het hele proces komt hier samen. Technisch ligt de lat hoog, maar de cultuur blijft nuchter en dichtbij. Je werkt met mensen die verantwoordelijkheid nemen, elkaar helpen en samen willen blijven verbeteren.

Seriously you?

We zoeken mensen die energie krijgen van complexe technologie en niet terugdeinzen voor een stevige uitdaging. Mensen die verantwoordelijkheid pakken, ideeën delen en samen willen blijven verbeteren. Herken jij jezelf daarin? Dan praten we graag verder.

title: Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:
Engineering Manager

Location: Remote - Europe (CET ±2 hours)

About FullEnrich:

Every go-to-market motion runs on data, but no single provider has ever had complete coverage. We solve that problem: instead of relying on a single data source, we orchestrate 20+ premium providers around the world, automatically querying them and verifying data in real-time until we find the best available contact information. The result is industry-leading coverage and data quality, helping sales and GTM teams connect with the right people faster.

What started as a better way to find emails and phone numbers has grown into a broader vision: becoming the trusted GTM data infrastructure layer powering modern revenue teams and AI agents. Today, more than 6,000 customers, including companies like AWS, Deel, HubSpot, Clay, Intercom, Unify,and Artisan, trust us to power their prospecting and enrichment.

Founded in Paris and now headquartered in San Francisco, we're a team of 50+ people across the US, Europe, LATAM, and Israel, growing quickly and building with speed, ownership, and ambition. That's where you come in.

The Role:

You'll be joining as an Engineering Manager, reporting directly to our VP of Engineering.

As FullEnrich continues to grow, we're investing in the engineering leadership and structure needed to support our next stage of growth. We're looking for someone who combines strong people leadership with technical depth, and who enjoys building high-performing teams, improving how engineers work, and creating the foundations for sustainable growth.

You'll initially lead a multidisciplinary team of up to ten engineers across backend, frontend, and data, taking ownership of their development, performance, and delivery. Working closely with Product Managers and engineering leadership, you'll help translate business priorities into achievable engineering objectives, ensuring teams have the clarity, support, and processes they need to deliver great work.

This is an opportunity to have a real impact on how our engineering organization evolves. As we scale toward 25 engineers, you'll help shape our squad structure, establish effective ways of working, and build an environment where engineers can grow and do their best work. You'll work closely with the VP of Engineering, CTO, and other Engineering Managers, with the autonomy to influence decisions and drive meaningful improvements across the organization.

What You'll Do:

People Leadership & Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop engineers through regular 1:1s, performance management, feedback, and career development.

  • Build a supportive, high-performing team environment where engineers have clear expectations, opportunities to grow, and the autonomy to do their best work.

  • Take ownership of team health, engagement, and retention, proactively identifying and addressing challenges.

Hiring & Team Growth

  • Own the engineering side of hiring for your squads, including defining requirements, setting assessment criteria, interviewing, and making hiring decisions.

  • Develop effective onboarding processes that help new engineers become productive and autonomous quickly.

  • Partner with engineering leadership to shape team structure, squad ownership, and hiring priorities as the organization scales.

Engineering Delivery & Execution

  • Partner with Product Managers to translate product and business priorities into clear engineering objectives, realistic roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.

  • Own engineering delivery across your squads, ensuring work is appropriately scoped, estimated, and delivered with clear accountability.

  • Identify and manage delivery risks, technical dependencies, and competing priorities, keeping stakeholders informed and addressing blockers early.

Engineering Processes & Continuous Improvement

  • Own and continuously improve how your squads operate, using our Discovery → Run lifecycle, inspired by Shape Up, and DORA metrics to measure delivery effectiveness.

  • Establish practical, scalable ways of working that improve predictability, collaboration, and engineering quality without introducing unnecessary bureaucracy.

  • Collaborate with other Engineering Managers and the VP of Engineering to evaluate and improve engineering processes across the wider organization.

Technical Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Provide technical guidance on architectural decisions, engineering trade-offs, and complex delivery challenges, ensuring teams make well-informed decisions.

  • Work closely with Product, Design, Support, Sales, and leadership to align engineering priorities with business needs.

  • Communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly, creating transparency and trust across teams and stakeholders.

Our Tech Stack

Our backend is built in Go (Golang), with Svelte on the frontend, PostgreSQL and OpenSearch for data, and DigitalOcean for cloud infrastructure. We use Docker, GitHub Actions, and Grafana to support deployment, automation, and observability, with a modular hexagonal monolith architecture.

You won't need to be hands-on with every technology, but you'll bring the technical understanding to challenge architectural decisions, navigate trade-offs, and support your engineers in solving complex problems.

What Success Looks Like:

By 3 months

  • You've built a strong understanding of our product, technology, engineering processes, and business objectives, establishing trusted relationships with your engineers and key stakeholders.

  • You've taken ownership of people management across your squads, with regular 1:1s, clear expectations, and an understanding of each engineer's strengths and development needs.

  • You've assessed current delivery practices, team structure, and performance, identifying opportunities to improve collaboration, predictability, and team effectiveness.

By 6 months

  • Your squads are operating with clear objectives, defined ownership, and measurable KPIs aligned with product and business priorities.

  • You've established effective delivery practices, with more predictable planning, proactive risk management, and improved visibility for stakeholders.

  • You've identified team capability gaps and are actively contributing to hiring, onboarding, and the development of engineers across your squads.

  • You're contributing meaningful improvements to engineering processes and organizational structure alongside the wider engineering management team.

By 12 months

  • Your squads consistently deliver against realistic, well-defined roadmaps, with clear accountability, effective collaboration, and measurable improvements in delivery performance.

  • Engineers have clear development paths, receive regular feedback, and feel supported in their growth, contributing to strong engagement and retention.

  • New engineers are onboarding efficiently and becoming productive quickly, supported by established processes and a clear engineering hiring bar.

  • You've helped shape a scalable engineering organization with well-defined squad ownership, effective ways of working, and stronger alignment between Engineering, Product, and the wider business.

  • Stakeholders have confidence in engineering delivery, with transparent communication, reliable planning, and fewer unexpected blockers.

What We're Looking For:

  • Proven experience directly managing and developing software engineers, ideally eight or more across multiple teams, within a growing engineering organization.

  • Demonstrated experience building or scaling engineering teams, including hiring, onboarding, performance management, and supporting engineers' career development.

  • A strong software engineering background with solid architectural fundamentals, enabling you to challenge technical decisions, understand trade-offs, and provide credible guidance.

  • Experience owning engineering delivery, translating product and business objectives into actionable plans, managing dependencies, and driving measurable outcomes.

  • A data-driven approach to engineering management, with experience using delivery metrics and team performance insights to identify and implement improvements.

  • The ability to establish effective engineering processes and ways of working that improve team performance without introducing unnecessary complexity.

  • Strong leadership and organizational skills, with the confidence to create structure, navigate ambiguity, and influence decisions in a scaling environment.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with experience collaborating effectively across distributed teams and cross-functional stakeholders.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience working with Go (Golang) or managing teams building Go-based applications.

  • Familiarity with Shape Up or similar appetite-driven development methodologies.

  • Experience using DORA metrics to measure and improve engineering delivery.

  • Knowledge of Team Topologies and experience shaping squad structures as engineering teams scale.

  • Experience scaling an engineering organization from approximately 10 to 25 engineers.

  • Background in B2B SaaS, data-intensive products, or API-first platforms.

The Hiring Process:

  • Introduction to FullEnrich with our Talent Team (30 mins) - A chance to learn more about you, introduce FullEnrich and the role, and explore whether there's a mutual fit.

  • Interview with the Hiring Manager (45 mins) - A chance for you to meet our VP of Engineering and walk through your background, the teams you've led, what you've built and broken along the way.

  • Engineering management case study (60 mins) - A practical session grounded in a real situation: a hiring decision, a delivery slipping, a process that isn't being followed, a performance conversation.

  • Final Interview with our CEO (45 min) – A chance for you to meet our CEO, Ben and have a conversation around FullEnrich's ambitions, how we work and what we're building together.

Benefits:

Your benefits package will reflect the requirements and market practices of the country in which you're employed, including applicable leave, healthcare, retirement and wellbeing benefits.

Full details will be shared during the hiring process.

FullEnrich is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.
