title: Principal Software Architect
descriptionHtml:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

Role Overview

Role:

We are looking for a Principal Software Architect to join our Compute Software organisation at IonQ. In this role, you will be responsible for developing and maintaining the architecture of the software that enables a quantum computer, from low level hardware control up to developer programming interfaces, contributing to the team’s mission of delivering a complete software product for a quantum computer.

You’ll play an important part in shaping the software and tools that support our work in building the world’s most advanced quantum systems. Our architecture now needs to evolve to support the next generation of our systems, and you will lead that work.

Responsibilities:

In this position, you will develop the software architecture covering real-time and non-real-time hardware management, low level orchestration and user interfaces for the current product and the future roadmap of products. You will also work with the technical leads from the development teams to support the effective development and delivery of a scalable solution that supports internal experimental scientists and external customers.

You’ll have the opportunity to develop an evolving software architecture to support a family of products, contributing directly to the success of the system software team in delivering a world leading quantum computer. You will coach and train technical leads in good architectural principles, and work closely with the infrastructure, firmware and compiler teams across the UK and the US.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Development and documentation of the system software architecture
  • Managing the evolving architecture across a family of products
  • Coordination with other architects across the whole of software and the wider system
  • Research and analysis to support future requirements elucidation
  • Coordination with technical leads to ensure that the design and implementation meets the intention of the architecture

Requirements:

To be successful, you will need prior experience of developing a large and scalable software architecture covering real-time requirements and distributed processing. We’re looking for someone who can think strategically at the architecture level, solve challenging technical issues, track the latest industry good practice and tools, and communicate those ideas and technologies to the wider software team.

You will work at the level of the whole system, describing each component, what it does and its constraints, and then handing the detailed design and implementation to the development teams rather than designing through code. A grounding in formal architecture methods and principles such as cohesion, coupling and encapsulation will help you succeed, as will experience of evolving an architecture that has to grow with the product. Our immediate focus is system software and lower level control; experience further up the software stack is an advantage.

You’d be a great fit with:

  • More than 10 years of software development experience, with more than 5 as a software architect
  • A clear understanding of software architecture principles
  • A background in real-time software development
  • Experience working on software projects written in Rust

Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment.

🌀 The Company

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

 

🎯 The Role

We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer to define and drive the technical direction of XTM One, Filigran's AI platform for threat informed defense and the agentic core of the XTM Suite.

XTM One creates and runs cybersecurity expert AI agents and dispatches their intelligence across OpenCTI, OpenAEV and OpenGRC. It also hosts the suite's shared commons (unified authentication, consolidated datasets, configuration) and ships both as SaaS and on premises. Every XTM product connects to it, which makes its architecture one of the most structuring technical decisions at Filigran.

title: Principal Thermal Solutions Engineer - Munich, Germany
descriptionHtml:
About Vinci

We are building Physics AI for hardware design. Our software platform helps hardware designers and physics simulation engineers explore, analyze, and optimize hardware systems, leveraging cutting-edge AI to deliver ultrafast, accurate physics intelligence within the realities of engineering design workflows.

Our first product bridges the gap between the accuracy & determinism of traditional simulation and the speed & scaling of AI, and is redefining how the world’s most advanced semiconductors are designed, verified, built, brought to market and integrated in complex systems.

Role Overview

As a pivotal leader within our European Forward Deployment team, you will drive the adoption of Vinci’s platform among the region's top engineering organizations. In this strategic role, you will build, mentor, and guide a high-performing team of thermal engineers dedicated to engaging prospective customers and demonstrating the transformative value of our software.

By acting as trusted technical advisors, you and your team will utilize deep simulation expertise to help enterprise customers validate and optimize complex, real-world designs. Through these collaborative engagements, you will champion Vinci's value proposition—showcasing how our platform delivers systemic improvements in thermal performance, product reliability, and accelerated time-to-market.

Leveraging strong fundamentals in thermal physics and cooling strategies, you will guide analyses of complex thermal management systems, fluid flow dynamics, and heat dissipation challenges. Your team will help customers evaluate critical factors such as thermal risk, component reliability, power density, and cooling efficiency to architect cutting-edge thermal management systems for next-generation hardware.

You will work closely with customer engineering teams to understand their technical challenges, provide expert guidance, and clearly articulate Vinci’s capabilities in solving real-world problems. Responsibilities

  • Maintain a strong understanding of competitive technologies, industry trends, and market positioning to communicate Vinci’s differentiators effectively.

Qualifications (Minimum Qualifications)

  • Education: Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related technical field.

  • Technical depth: Expert-level mastery of commercial simulation software (Flotherm, Ansys Icepak/Fluent, Simcenter STAR-CCM+, or equivalent), with 15+ years of hands-on experience in thermal management and cooling solutions — either as a practitioner running simulations, or as a technical account manager for commercial physics simulation software.

  • Customer Engagement: Prior experience in dedicated customer-facing roles, with a strong ability to build trust and manage engineering client relationships.

  • Automation & Scripting: Practical programming experience using Python or C++ to automate workflows or parse simulation data.

  • Leadership Impact: Proven track record of prior managerial or technical leadership experience, with the ability to scale, mentor, and drive execution across engineering teams.

  • Communication: Elite interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to distill complex physics and simulation results into clear, high-impact narratives for both deep technical panels and business-oriented executives.

Preferred (Desirable Differentiators)

  • Multiphysics Breadth: Familiarity with structural mechanical simulations (FEA/stress) and/or Electrical Signal Integrity and Power Integrity (SI/PI) workflows.

  • Commercial Track Record: Direct experience commercializing technical software—ideally electronic design automation (EDA) or CAE simulation tools—into major semiconductor and electronics enterprises.

  • Go-To-Market Experience: Prior experience explicitly within technical pre-sales, application engineering (FAE), or strategic technical sales environments.

  • Emerging Tech Adjacency: Ability to rapidly adopt and champion next-generation, physics-based workflows and AI-assisted design or simulation tools.

You will also help shape how we build software with AI agents, translating requirements into working code and establishing the guardrails, automated tests and review habits that keep quality high when code is AI-assisted. You remain responsible for every line you ship, whether you or an agent wrote it.

The role

We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it.

You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built.

Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are.

  • Product: You build best in class products for the core jobs in freight forwarding, one job at a time. You work as a design partner with our customers to understand the work deeply, turn that understanding into a product they would choose over anything else, and feed what you learn back into the platform everyone builds on.

  • AI: You raise the ceiling on what our AI can do and the floor on how reliably it does it. That spans high volume tasks like classification and extraction and deep workflow tasks that run for hours. You design for performance, reliability, explainability and control, set up the gyms and evals to measure them, and build the harness that runs our agents in all of our products.

  • Platform: You own the foundation every product stands on: the runtime for thousands of concurrent agents and workflows, the way they communicate and scale, the controls for how they access data with permissions that hold, and the observability to see and measure all of it. You ensure the rest of the team can move fast without fear.

     

What we look for

  • A spike, with evidence. Something you have been exceptional at and proof of it. We hire on slope rather than years, so there is no experience threshold in either direction.

  • Strong fundamentals. In the AI-assisted era, having good technical judgement is key. You have shipped production systems people depend on, seen them fail and learned from it.

  • High agency and ownership. You take an ambiguous problem, make a call, and see it through.

  • Humility and learning velocity. You want to get better and you change your mind when the evidence says so.

  • Interest in the problem. You do not need a freight background, but you need to find messy real-world operations interesting rather than a chore.

     

Why join

You will shape the product, the architecture and the company, working alongside an engineering team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will work directly with the businesses using what you build, on AI applied to an industry that has resisted software for decades. You will get meaningful equity, so when this works you share in it.

title: Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

How we work

We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder, and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work.

We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods, usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart.

We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move.

Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest.

A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer.

The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 2, that looks like this:

 

What you'll be doing

  • Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion.

  • Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced.

  • Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.

  • Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

  • Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you.

  • Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered.

  • Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve.

  • Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps.

  • Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to.

  • Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce.

  • Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity.

  • Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them.

 

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

 

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Interview process

  1. Initial chat with our Talent team

  2. Lead Hirer Interview

  3. Live AI Skills Assessment

  4. Values Interview with the CPTO

  5. Meet the CEO

 

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

 

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

title: Product Integration Engineer, Defence
descriptionHtml:
We're looking for a Product Integration Engineer to develop and prove out our products with military customers, starting with the Field Operator HUD (FOH): a head-mounted, always-on visual intelligence system built from Distance hardware, a HUD operating system and AI-assisted data processing that pulls sensor, feeds and command-and-control into the operator's field of view. Your job is to make it work on a specific customer's platform, in the field, not just on a bench, as part of our core R&D team. If you're a hands-on generalist who knows VR or XR and would rather be where the tech meets the user than stuck at a desk, this one's for you.

WHY DISTANCE?

At Distance Technologies, the problem we're solving is simple to state and hard to solve: the amount of data in the world is endless, but human capacity is not. We are building a fundamentally new perception layer between humans and machines, transforming transparent surfaces into interfaces unlike the world has ever seen. Think of the windscreen of a car, the visor of a helmet, or a sight device, each becoming a new front-end for AI. The way we turn bits and atoms into expanded human perception is protected by over 50 granted international patent families. We build it for two demanding worlds: defence and automotive. And we build it from a single foundation fusing software, hardware and computational optics.

There are 60 of us today, with decades-long experience building world's best products, optics, and open-source operating systems. We partner and build with globally leading companies like KIA, Supacat, and Galvion, and we were Google Ventures' first investment in Finland.

THE ROLE

The FOH is already in field trials with military users. Your first project is getting it working with British Army equipment and defence primes, building the integration around what the customer actually needs. As our product line grows you'll take on a widening set of customer integrations across our defence work, each one a different platform, stack and set of interfaces.

Your core responsibilities include:

  • Owning customer integrations end to end. Make the FOH work inside a customer's platform: adapt the software, wire it into their sensors, displays, video and connectivity, and get it demo- and trial-ready. Prototype fast in dedicated environments to prove value with a client before it hits the shared codebase.

  • Being Distance in the field. Join demos, trials and exercises with defence clients, support on-site deployments when needed, and bring back what you see and hear on real kit.

  • Bridging the field and the core. Turn what customers need into concrete integration work with the R&D and commercial teams, spot what should become shared product capability, and feed it into the roadmap and, eventually, the shared codebase.

You won't be a satellite. You'll join the software standups and reviews and be a real part of R&D.

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

  • Your work ships and gets used. What you integrate goes into real kit already in trials with military users, and what you learn from demos, trials and exercises with them feeds straight back into the product.

  • You own the whole thread. From first prototype to working integration in the field, it's yours, not passed between five teams.

  • New display tech. Glasses-free computational optics and a see-through HUD, the kind of problem you won't find at most XR jobs.

  • A small team backed to move fast. Around 60 of us, Google Ventures' first investment in Finland, and flat enough that your calls count.

OUR EXPECTATIONS

What we're looking for:

  • A builder, not a passenger: a hands-on self-starter who takes ownership, works things out when docs are missing, and would rather be with a customer or in the field than at a desk.

  • At least a couple of years of software engineering experience with VR or XR, plus generalist instincts.

  • Comfort across a mixed software stack. You've worked with some of C++, Unity and embedded, and you pick up the rest quickly.

  • Some exposure to electrical integration or software-to-hardware interfaces. We're not expecting deep hardware experience on top of strong software.

  • You're at home in prototype and integration work: incomplete docs, customer-specific stacks, messy interfaces.

  • Good with clients, and happy to be the person representing Distance at a demo or trial.

  • Willing to travel within the UK when needed, and to Finland now and then.

It's a bonus, though not required, if you've worked with HMDs, wearable displays or spatial computing, know C++ for integration and application development, can stand up a UI or application stack for quick situational-awareness or demo prototypes, are comfortable with embedded or Linux at integration level, or have seen sensor, display and video interfaces at system level.

You'll be based within commuting distance of the Bath office and in the office two to three days a week. Our working language is English.

title: Product Manager – Cross-Border Payments & Digital Assets
descriptionHtml:
About us

ClearBank was built on the belief that banking infrastructure should enable progress, not slow it down. Our clients, from fintechs and digital asset businesses to banks and financial institutions, use our technology and APIs to power innovative banking and payment propositions.

But we wouldn’t be ClearBank without our people. They’re what powers our technology and the reason we love what we do every day. We’re a group of ambitious, curious people who aren’t afraid to challenge the status quo. We believe in fairness, autonomy and choice, empowering our people with the tools and opportunities to learn, grow and contribute to the success of ClearBank and our clients.

About you

You’ll be joining the Product team as a Product Manager – Cross-Border Payments & Digital Assets, reporting to the Head of Product, Cross-Border Payments and Foreign Exchange.

This is an exciting opportunity to help shape ClearBank’s next generation of international payments and digital asset propositions.

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on Product Manager who can operate at the intersection of cross-border payments, banking infrastructure and digital assets. You’ll help develop propositions that enable our clients to move money internationally through both traditional payment infrastructure and emerging digital asset and stablecoin rails.

You’ll be comfortable taking complex opportunities from discovery through to launch, working across Product, Engineering, Operations, Treasury, Financial Crime, Compliance, Risk and Commercial teams.

You’ll combine strong customer understanding with commercial and technical thinking, translating market opportunities and complex payment flows into scalable products that solve genuine customer problems.

You will be

As Product Manager, you’ll own key initiatives across cross-border payments and digital assets, helping define the product strategy, roadmap and delivery priorities.

You’ll work closely with Engineering and cross-functional teams to understand customer problems, define requirements and take new capabilities from discovery and design through delivery, pilot and commercial launch.

Within cross-border payments, this could include capabilities covering international payment corridors, payment providers and networks, multi-currency payment flows, FX-enabled payments and alternative payment rails.

Within Digital Assets, the role will contribute to developing propositions including stablecoin payments, stablecoin minting and redemption, fiat-to-digital-asset connectivity, custody and tokenisation opportunities

A major part of the role will be connecting these two worlds and exploring how emerging digital asset infrastructure can complement traditional correspondent banking and payment networks to deliver faster, more efficient and scalable global payment propositions.

You’ll also work directly with customers, partners and internal stakeholders to validate propositions and ensure they are commercially viable, operationally scalable and aligned with ClearBank’s risk and regulatory requirements.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute product roadmaps in partnership with the Head of Product, translating strategic objectives into clear priorities and measurable outcomes.

  • Own product initiatives across the full lifecycle, from customer discovery and business case development through design, delivery, pilot, launch and ongoing optimisation.

  • Develop and enhance ClearBank’s cross-border payment propositions, including international payment corridors, payment providers, payment networks and new payment rails.

  • Help develop ClearBank’s Digital Assets proposition, including stablecoin payments, minting and redemption, fiat/stablecoin interoperability, custody and tokenisation-related opportunities.

  • Evaluate how traditional correspondent banking, payment networks and blockchain-based rails can be used individually or together to improve international payment propositions.

  • Work closely with Engineering, Architecture and Business Analysis teams to translate customer and business problems into clearly defined product and technology requirements.

  • Lead product discovery with existing and prospective clients to understand customer pain points, underlying use cases and future requirements.

  • Evaluate potential banking, payment and digital asset partners, considering product capability, coverage, commercial model, technology integration and customer proposition.

  • Build business cases and support product-level commercial management, including pricing, volumes, costs, revenue opportunities and product economics.

  • Work closely with Treasury, Operations, Financial Crime, Compliance, Legal and Risk teams to ensure new propositions can operate safely and effectively within ClearBank’s risk appetite and regulatory obligations.

  • Develop appropriate operating models and ensure operational processes, controls and customer journeys are ready ahead of product launch.

Core Skills and Experience

  • Strong Product Management experience within payments, banking, fintech or financial infrastructure.

  • Good understanding of cross-border payments, including correspondent banking, international payment flows and the challenges associated with moving money across currencies and jurisdictions.

  • Experience taking complex financial products from discovery through delivery and launch.

  • Demonstrable experience working with Engineering teams in an Agile product environment.

  • Strong customer-discovery skills, with the ability to turn customer problems and use cases into clear product requirements and priorities.

  • Strong commercial mindset, with experience considering pricing, costs, volumes, unit economics and business cases when making product decisions.

  • Ability to understand complex end-to-end payment flows and translate them into clear product, technical and operational requirements.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to structure ambiguous problems and recommend pragmatic solutions.

  • Experience working across multidisciplinary teams including Engineering, Operations, Compliance, Financial Crime, Treasury, Risk and Commercial functions.

  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to explain complex payment or technology concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • A proactive, hands-on approach with strong ownership and accountability.

A little bit more about us! 

ClearBank is Where You Can belong: 

At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 

  • 42% of our senior management roles are held by women 

  • Our enhanced family leave policies

  • Launching our partnership with Code First Girls 

  • Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group 

Our hiring process and what you can expect:

Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; 

Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); 

First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams.  

Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team.

Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes.  

Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! 

Our commitment to you as a candidate: 

We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time.  

We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully.  

We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon!  

Equal Opportunities

ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. 

ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation. 

As part of the Company’s commitment to equal employment opportunity, we provide reasonable adjustments, to candidates during the recruitment process, including to individuals with disabilities. We want to create a safe space that welcomes everyone so please let us know how we can accommodate you. In case you have any accessibility requirements you can share that with our Talent Acquisition team prior to your interview stage, if applicable. 

The legal bit

By submitting your CV to ClearBank Limited you are providing your consent for us to use the information you provide for recruitment purposes. For more information on how we manage your data go and check out our Candidate Privacy Notice on the ClearBank website to see how we process, manage and look after your data. You are also allowing us to communicate with you by email and telephone for recruitment purposes.

title: Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

And we’re a long way from done!

THE ROLE

Buying and selling a car should feel like one seamless motion for a dealer, not two separate systems. Right now it's the opposite: a dealer buys through us, then has to manage collection, payment and resale largely on their own, stitching together workflows across multiple platforms and channels, much of it manual.

For a dealer, speed is money. Every extra day a car sits before it's collected, priced, and paid for is a day of depreciation, tied-up capital, and a missed chance to buy the next one.If we can get a dealer from 'I've bought this car' to 'it's ready and paid for' faster through transport and collections, quicker final pricing, and Wallet, we make them more profitable. A dealer who's more profitable because of Carwow has little reason to go elsewhere: they'll lean on us more, and churn less.

This role owns that last-mile agenda: getting cars collected quickly, resolving final price without friction, and making Wallet work the way dealers expect it to. This team sits across our ambitions to make car changing a seamless journey, this role's job is the handover itself: the operational moment between buying and being ready to sell again. This is also a moment where AI changes what's possible. Dealers are already asking for smarter scheduling, less manual chasing, and tools that reduce the overhead of running a business. We want to build those things. The PM in this role will need the curiosity to explore what that could look like, and the rigour to distinguish genuine value from noise. If you want to own an operational product area end to end, work with some of the most sophisticated buyers in UK retail, and build things that have a direct line to commercial outcomes, this is it.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • Product Strategy & Execution:

    • Own the product direction for Carwow's dealer-facing product, defining what we build, in what order, and why

    • Lead discovery work with dealers, interviews, on-site visits, data analysis to build a precise understanding of where we can add the most value

    • Identify and test opportunities to bring AI into dealer workflows: smarter recommendations, vehicle pricing, performance insights that actually change behaviour

    • Collaborate with Tech Lead, Designer, and Engineers to ship well-scoped solutions with clear success metrics

    • Manage the backlog with commercial awareness prioritising work that drives engagement, retention, and revenue, not just activity

  • Partner Engagement & Insight:

    • Build relationships with key dealer partners and use those relationships to validate product direction before we build

    • Work with Account Management and Sales to understand what's driving churn, what's blocking adoption, and what would make carwow stickier

    • Translate qualitative partner feedback into structured product insight; don't just collect opinions, turn them into decisions

  • Cross-functional Leadership:

    • Work across product, engineering, commercial, and marketing to align on priorities and ship coherently

    • Communicate strategy and trade-offs clearly to leadership and stakeholders, written as well as verbal

    • Support the commercial team on partner conversations where product context matters: capability deep-dives, roadmap discussions, strategic accounts

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 1.5+ years of product management experience in a B2B or SaaS environment, with evidence of improving engagement or retention metrics

  • Hands-on experience with product discovery: you run your own interviews, interrogate your own data, and form your own hypotheses rather than waiting for research to land in your inbox

title: Product Marketing Manager - Care Providers & Health
descriptionHtml:
Finance Deserves Better

Finance teams at fast-growing companies run global, real-time businesses on a patchwork of legacy ERPs and point solutions. Every new entity, site or tool adds another system to stitch together and another hire to keep the numbers reconciled.

Light gives them a way out. We build the finance solution that lets finance teams have it all, through three parts that work as one:

  • Our ledger records every transaction across every entity in real time, so the numbers hold up from day one.

  • Our apps adapt Light to how each business runs, from procurement to billing to reporting.

  • Our agents operate the repetitive work that used to need another hire, so finance teams spend their time on the decisions that matter.

Today we run the finance function for companies like Lovable, Legora and Keyshot, with backing from Atomico, Balderton, Seedcamp, Cherry and Entrée. Now we’re taking Light into specific industries, with the ambition of becoming the operating layer each one runs on. Care homes and clinics sit among our priority sectors.

The Role

We’re looking for a Product Marketing Manager to go deep on health, starting with groups that run several care homes, clinics or practices, and work out how Light wins there.

These groups carry the finance problems of any multi-entity business, plus funding models, regulation and workflows of their own. Your job is to understand these buyers better than anyone at Light, turn what you learn into positioning and proof our sales team can use, and build the playbook we follow to scale our go-to-market across the sector.

You’ll sit in our product marketing team and work side by side with our Care and Health Sales Managers, with support from demand generation, field marketing and product.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Interviewing customers, prospects and specialist partners to learn how care home groups and clinics buy, what makes them change and where their finance workflows break.

  • Mapping the market with Sales: which segments we go after first, which we test, and which we leave for later.

  • Turning what you learn into positioning, messaging and competitive arguments that hold up in front of an operator or a finance director.

  • Building the sales kit, from customer stories and demo narratives to objection handling and one-pagers, so our reps speak the sector’s language.

  • Training sales reps and SDRs on the buyers, workflows and vocabulary of each segment, and joining customer calls to hear what lands.

  • Bringing the sector’s requirements back to Product, and separating the needs that recur from the one-off requests.

  • Giving demand generation and field marketing the insight, content and angles they need for sector campaigns and events, and tracking what turns into pipeline.

  • Writing down what works, so the next sector we enter starts from a playbook rather than a blank page.

What We Think* You’ll Need

  • Product marketing experience at a B2B SaaS company, with a track record of taking a product or segment from insight to launch to sales adoption.

  • A habit of talking to customers, and the judgement to turn interviews into clear positioning.

  • Experience in health, care or a closely related sector helps. Curiosity and the speed to earn credibility with operators matter more.

  • Strong writing, from a sharp one-pager to a customer story people want to share.

  • Comfort working with Sales every day, and a feel for what helps a rep win a deal.

  • An analytical streak. You can read funnel data, spot where deals stall and test why.

  • Daily use of AI for research, writing and analysis, with the discipline to check what it tells you.

  • A can-do, empathetic and collaborative spirit. No brilliant jerks here, please.

*If the core of the role sounds compelling but you don’t tick every box, we’d still love for you to reach out and convince us you’re the right person.

The Good Stuff

🏢 A five-day, in-office culture with a high-density team in London.
💸 A competitive salary and potential stock options.
🏝 25 days of annual leave plus UK public holidays.
🥳 Regular socials and two company offsites a year. The last 2 were in Tuscany & Provence!
🌍 Travel to Copenhagen, Munich, New York, Paris and wherever care homes and clinics do business.
🚀 The chance to define how Light wins in a sector from its first deals.

Light is an equal opportunity employer.

The Famous Last Words

Care home groups and clinics run complex businesses on finance tools that weren’t built for them. We want to change that, and we want you to learn the sector inside out and show us how. When you apply, tell us about a segment you got to know from scratch: how you learned it, what you changed because of it, and how you helped Sales win there.

title: Product Marketing Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Nabla

Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes:

Ambient AI documentation that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes.

AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools embedded directly within EHR systems.

Agentic AI capabilities that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks.

Enterprise-grade infrastructure built for secure deployment across health systems.

About the Role

The Product Marketing Manager will own how Nabla positions, launches, and drives adoption of the product with clinicians across their entire journey — from onboarding and activation through engagement and retention.

This is product marketing where the message ships directly to the user. You own the narrative for every new feature launch, then own the in-app and email programs that turn that narrative into activation.

You'll define the segmentation, write the positioning, ship the campaigns, and measure whether they actually moved adoption.

Userpilot is in place, but everything around it still needs to be built: the activation and adoption strategy, in-app and email templates, segmentation, cohort analysis, the process with Product Marketing peers, CSM, PM, and Design, and the campaign calendar.

This is a hands-on, highly operational PMM role. We need someone who lives in the tools, is data-driven, can test fast, structure the process, and turn usage insights into concrete positioning and messaging decisions.

Userpilot is the first step. Over time, this person will take ownership of the full communication stack across email, in-app, and other channels. The role works extremely closely with Product Marketing peers, Design, PM, Data, and Product Ops.

Nabla serves two distinct audiences, and lifecycle programs must work for both:

  • Self-serve clinicians, who discover, activate, and adopt the product largely on their own. Here, automated email and in-app communication carries most of the relationship — your messaging is the go-to-market motion.

  • Mid-market and enterprise health systems, managed by CSMs. Here the human relationship leads, and your programs must arm and reinforce the CSM — giving them timing, context, and content, never working around them.

You'll design each lifecycle so the right channel leads for each segment. On top of this, healthtech is a highly regulated industry with demanding clients: every communication must meet a high bar for accuracy, security, and professionalism, while still feeling personal and useful to busy clinicians.

Responsibilities

Feature Launch Positioning & Activation

  • Own weekly in-app launch communication for new features, end to end and at a fast cadence

  • Define the positioning and messaging for each release — what it is, why a clinician should care, what changes in their day

  • Design the in-app experience (placement, format, flow) for each launch

  • Validate messaging with Product Marketing peers, PM, and Design before shipping

  • Launch on time and coordinate across the relevant teams

  • Track performance (reach, engagement, adoption) for every launch and iterate quickly on results

  • Stay highly reactive to the product roadmap, turning new releases into clear, well-timed clinician communication

Lifecycle Strategy and Execution

  • Own the full lifecycle strategy across onboarding, activation, engagement, and retention, ensuring each stage of the practitioner journey is intentional, personalized, and measurable

  • Tailor segmentation, messaging, and cadence to the distinct needs of each segment:

    • For self-serve, build automated email and in-app programs that drive activation, adoption, and retention with minimal human touch

    • For mid-market and enterprise, build programs that complement and support CSMs

  • Direct and execute creative strategy for lifecycle channels — briefing, reviewing, and optimizing copy and design for brand consistency and message effectiveness

  • Build and maintain a clear campaign calendar across functions

Experimentation and Analytics

  • Lead a rigorous experimentation roadmap: A/B and multivariate testing of messaging, creative, cadence, segmentation, and value propositions

  • Define and own lifecycle KPIs, building reporting frameworks and sharing regular performance insights with marketing and cross-functional leadership

  • Partner with Data and Analytics on audience segmentation, behavioral signals, and AI-driven insights to enhance personalization at scale

  • Turn cohort and usage insights into concrete messaging and product-marketing actions

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with Product Marketing peers, Design, PM, Data, Product Ops, Clinical, and Brand to align lifecycle programs with broader business goals and the practitioner experience

  • Establish a clear, repeatable process across Product Marketing, CSM, PM, and Design for planning and shipping campaigns

  • Ensure all programs are developed and executed in compliance with HIPAA and applicable federal and state laws, partnering with Legal and Compliance as needed

Operations and Tooling

  • Take ownership of the full communication stack, starting with Userpilot

  • Evaluate and manage lifecycle marketing technology partnerships, recommending optimizations as we scale

  • Build and maintain process documentation, campaign playbooks, and training materials on internal platforms

  • Leverage AI tools as a core part of daily work (drafting, research, iteration) to improve efficiency, quality, and decision-making

What We Are Looking For

  • 3-5 years in B2B product marketing, lifecycle marketing, or product-led growth marketing, including hands-on ownership of in-app channels

  • Proven ability to craft positioning and messaging for product launches and to ship it yourself, not hand it off

  • Deep expertise across the full post-signup funnel (onboarding, activation, engagement, retention)

  • Strong Product DNA, with sharp attention to user workflows and the details that shape the product experience

  • Strong strategic and analytical thinking, with the ability to translate complex data into clear hypotheses, actionable insights, and business recommendations

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; ability to manage stakeholder expectations, influence without authority, and build alignment across diverse teams

  • Track record of building and scaling programs that drove measurable growth in adoption, engagement, and retention

  • Comfortable in a highly regulated, high-stakes industry (healthtech) with demanding clients, where accuracy, security, and compliance are non-negotiable

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience with Userpilot and HubSpot

  • Familiarity with Looker, Tableau, Mixpanel, Amplitude, or similar

  • Experience in a regulated industry: healthcare, behavioral health, or health-adjacent

  • Experience with AI-powered personalization, segmentation tools, or ML-informed campaign optimization

  • Experience marketing to a professional or clinical end user

Life at Nabla

When you join Nabla, you join a team that is driven by excellence, curiousity, and kindness. Together, we’re committed to making clinicians’ lives easier and improving healthcare experiences for everyone. We believe clinicians should be able to focus on what they were trained to do, caring for their patients, and that no patient should feel their visit was rushed.

We work hard and make time to have fun, too. Our #nablabla channel is just as active as #feature-show-off. We support well-being with workday activities at least three times a week; choose from yoga, running, Pilates, or HIIT. We also host regular off-sites, meet up across New York, Paris, San Francisco, and other cities, and keep the chocolate and nuts well stocked.

If this sounds like an environment where you’ll thrive, we look forward to reading your application.

Our Values at Nabla

Joining Nabla means being part of a team that shares a commitment to excellence, humility, growth, and inclusion.

Every day is a new chance to excel

We aim for nothing less than the best and are willing to put in the effort and dedication required to exceed standards. We learn from yesterday’s failures and do better every day.

Stay humble

There’s no place for ego in our team. Our collective success is more important than individual achievements. We see humility as wisdom — keeping focus on the bigger picture.

Feedback is a gift

We embrace feedback and foster a culture of trust and respect that helps everyone grow. We communicate openly about both achievements and challenges, and we actively involve each other in finding solutions.

Committed to diversity

We recognize the ongoing challenge of diversity in tech. Our responsibility starts with fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels empowered to be their authentic selves and do their best work.

Diversity & Inclusion

Diversity and inclusivity are fundamental values at Nabla. We embrace individuals from various backgrounds, including race, gender, educational history, sexual orientation, and beyond.

As an equal opportunity employer, we actively seek out and welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, believing that a wide range of perspectives enriches our team and enhances our ability to innovate and thrive.

Avoid recruitment scams: Stay safe and informed

There is an active employment and financial scam which uses Nabla to collect personal information. If you’re contacted by a Nabla recruiter, please ensure they are utilizing a nabla.com email address. We will never ask for the exchange of any money or credit card details during the recruitment process. Nabla utilizes a hiring platform for all applications; please be aware of any suspicious email activity. You can find more information following this link.


Nabla does not accept unsolicited CVs from recruiters or employment agencies in response to the Nabla Careers page or a Nabla social media post. Any unsolicited CVs, including those submitted directly to hiring managers, are deemed to be the property of Nabla.

title: Public Sector Sales Lead
descriptionHtml:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As Anthropic's Public Sector Sales Lead for France, you will be the face of Anthropic to the French State. This is a founding, zero-to-one role: there is no public sector team in France today, and you will build our strategy, our routes to market and our first strategic relationships from the ground up. Reporting to our EMEA South leadership, you will lead the adoption of safe, frontier AI across central government, starting with the largest ministries. You will work hand in hand with our Public Policy lead in Paris, because in few companies is policy as central to the mission as it is at Anthropic, and with Partnerships, Legal, Security and Product to put in place the commercial and compliance frameworks the State needs in order to work with us at scale.

This is a senior individual contributor role. We expect you to have run a public sector business and led teams, and to be energised by stepping back into a hands-on seat where you build it yourself and where the size of your team says nothing about the size of your scope. In the first year, success is measured less by a large number and more by putting Anthropic on the map with the French State: a clear strategy, the right foundations and our first strategic agreements.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own Anthropic's public sector go-to-market strategy for France: where we play first, how we win, and what we need to build to get there
  • Be the senior face of Anthropic to the French State, building trusted relationships with ministerial cabinets, senior officials and digital and technology leaders across the largest ministries, including defence, finance and justice
  • Own the full sales cycle on our first strategic public sector opportunities, from first engagement through procurement route, close, deployment and expansion
  • Work with Partnerships, Legal and Finance to put in place the routes to market the State needs, including resale and partner channels, framework agreements and central purchasing bodies such as UGAP
  • Partner day to day with our Public Policy lead in France so that commercial and policy engagement reinforce each other, and stay aligned with French and European AI strategy and regulation
  • Lead the conversation with customers on data sovereignty, security and compliance (for example SecNumCloud and the State's cloud doctrine), and work with Security, Legal and Product on how we meet those requirements
  • Prove value with customers alongside a shared Applied AI architect, cloud providers and systems integrators, doing much of the groundwork yourself in the early stages
  • Learn from and contribute to our UK and US public sector teams, bringing what works to France and sharing what you learn
  • Create the playbooks, references and operating rhythm that will let us scale a public sector team in France over time

You may be a good fit if you have

  • 15+ years in enterprise technology sales, including significant time running a public sector business unit or leading sales teams that sell to French central government
  • The appetite to move from a leadership role into a hands-on senior individual contributor role with no team at the outset
  • Evidence that you thrive building from zero: a new market, a new business line or an early-stage company, where systems, processes and support were not yet in place
  • A track record of landing large, complex and genuinely transformative agreements with major ministries, as the person leading the deal
  • A deep, senior network across central government, and the credibility to engage at director and cabinet level as well as with technical teams
  • Practical command of French public procurement, including tenders, framework agreements, central purchasing bodies and partner or resale routes
  • Real expertise in data sovereignty, security and compliance requirements in the French State, and experience leading those conversations with customers
  • Experience of, or a clear aptitude for, working closely with public policy or government affairs colleagues
  • Ownership and resilience: you treat what is missing as something to build, and you bring colleagues with you to build it
  • The technical curiosity to learn our products in depth and hold credible conversations with both engineering leaders and senior officials
  • Fluent French and English, with excellent written and spoken communication in both
  • Willingness to go through French security clearance (habilitation) should specific accounts require it 
  • A genuine commitment to safe and beneficial AI, and the ability to articulate why it matters for public institutions

À propos du poste

En tant que Responsable des ventes secteur public d'Anthropic pour la France, vous incarnerez Anthropic auprès de l'État français. Il s'agit d'un poste fondateur, à construire de zéro : il n'existe aujourd'hui aucune équipe secteur public en France, et vous bâtirez notre stratégie, nos voies d'accès au marché et nos premières relations stratégiques en partant d'une page blanche. Ce poste est rattaché à la direction EMEA Sud. Vous piloterez l'adoption d'une IA de pointe et sûre au sein de l'administration centrale, en commençant par les plus grands ministères. Vous travaillerez main dans la main avec notre responsable des affaires publiques à Paris — dans peu d'entreprises les politiques publiques sont aussi centrales à la mission que chez Anthropic — ainsi qu'avec les équipes Partenariats, Juridique, Sécurité et Produit, afin de mettre en place les cadres commerciaux et de conformité dont l'État a besoin pour travailler avec nous à grande échelle.

Il s'agit d'un poste senior de contribution individuelle. Nous attendons de vous que vous ayez dirigé une activité secteur public et encadré des équipes, et que la perspective de revenir à un poste pleinement opérationnel vous enthousiasme : un poste où vous construisez vous-même, et où la taille de votre équipe ne dit rien de l'étendue de votre périmètre. La première année, la réussite se mesurera moins à un grand chiffre qu'à votre capacité à installer Anthropic auprès de l'État français : une stratégie claire, les bonnes fondations et nos premiers accords stratégiques.

Responsabilités

  • Définir et porter la stratégie de mise sur le marché d'Anthropic pour le secteur public en France : nos premiers terrains d'action, nos leviers de succès et ce qu'il nous faut construire pour y parvenir
  • Incarner Anthropic au plus haut niveau auprès de l'État français, en nouant des relations de confiance avec les cabinets ministériels, les cadres dirigeants de l'administration et les responsables du numérique et de la technologie des plus grands ministères, dont la défense, les finances et la justice
  • Piloter l'intégralité du cycle de vente sur nos premières opportunités stratégiques dans le secteur public, du premier contact au choix de la voie de passation, jusqu'à la signature, au déploiement et à l'extension
  • Travailler avec les équipes Partenariats, Juridique et Finance pour mettre en place les voies d'accès au marché dont l'État a besoin : canaux de revente et de partenariat, accords-cadres et centrales d'achat telles que l'UGAP
  • Collaborer au quotidien avec notre responsable des affaires publiques en France, pour que les démarches commerciales et politiques se renforcent mutuellement, en cohérence avec la stratégie et la réglementation française et européenne en matière d'IA
  • Mener les échanges clients sur la souveraineté des données, la sécurité et la conformité (par exemple SecNumCloud et la doctrine « cloud au centre »), et travailler avec les équipes Sécurité, Juridique et Produit sur la façon dont nous répondons à ces exigences
  • Démontrer la valeur auprès des clients en vous appuyant sur une expertise d'architecture Applied AI mutualisée, sur les fournisseurs cloud et sur les intégrateurs, en réalisant vous-même une grande part du travail de terrain dans les premiers temps
  • Apprendre de nos équipes secteur public au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis et contribuer à leur travail, en important en France ce qui fonctionne et en partageant vos enseignements
  • Créer les playbooks, les références clients et le rythme opérationnel qui nous permettront de faire grandir une équipe secteur public en France

Ce poste peut vous correspondre si vous réunissez

  • Plus de 15 ans dans la vente de technologies aux grandes organisations, dont une période significative à la tête d'une activité secteur public ou à l'encadrement d'équipes commerciales à destination de l'administration centrale française
  • L'envie de passer d'un poste d'encadrement à un poste senior pleinement opérationnel, en contribution individuelle et sans équipe au départ
  • Un parcours qui montre que vous vous épanouissez en construisant à partir de zéro : un nouveau marché, une nouvelle ligne d'activité ou une entreprise à ses débuts, là où les systèmes, les processus et les soutiens n'existaient pas encore
  • Des accords majeurs, complexes et réellement transformateurs conclus avec de grands ministères à votre actif, en étant la personne à la tête de la négociation
  • Un réseau dense et de haut niveau au sein de l'administration centrale, et la crédibilité nécessaire pour échanger au niveau des directions et des cabinets comme avec les équipes techniques
  • Une maîtrise concrète de la commande publique française : appels d'offres, accords-cadres, centrales d'achat et voies de partenariat ou de revente
  • Une véritable expertise des exigences de souveraineté des données, de sécurité et de conformité au sein de l'État français, et l'expérience de ces échanges avec les clients
  • L'expérience — ou une aptitude manifeste — du travail en étroite collaboration avec les équipes affaires publiques ou relations institutionnelles
  • Le sens de la responsabilité et la ténacité : ce qui manque est pour vous quelque chose à construire, et vous embarquez vos collègues dans cette construction
  • La curiosité technique nécessaire pour apprendre nos produits en profondeur et tenir des échanges crédibles aussi bien avec les responsables d'ingénierie qu'avec les responsables publics de haut niveau
  • Un français et un anglais courants, avec une excellente expression écrite et orale dans les deux langues
  • La disponibilité pour engager une procédure d'habilitation de sécurité si certains comptes l'exigent
  • Un engagement sincère en faveur d'une IA sûre et bénéfique, et la capacité d'expliquer pourquoi cela compte pour les institutions publiques

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Quality Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Isembard

Isembard is building a network of high-performance factories for critical industries. We combine advanced machine tools, robotics and our own software, MasonOS, to make precision components for aerospace, defence, energy and frontier technology companies, with factories across the UK, US, Germany and France. Our mission is to forge industrial acceleration.

The role

Quality is where a precision factory earns its customers or loses them. This role owns quality control at our London factory, on parts going to aerospace, defence, energy and other critical industries.

It is hands-on inspection and engineering judgement in equal measure. Beyond the bench, you will build the procedures and controls that let the factory grow without inspection becoming the bottleneck.

What you'll do

  • Inspect parts entering QC after cleaning, running visual and dimensional checks with the right tooling.

  • Read drawings and part requirements correctly, and disposition rework and nonconforming parts.

  • Keep MasonOS and FlatBOM accurate. The rest of the factory plans against what you record.

  • Build quality procedures and governance so quality is controlled in the process, not only found at final inspection.

  • Improve QC systems and SOPs, and strengthen the handoffs into and out of quality.

What we're looking for

  • An engineering degree or equivalent technical experience.

  • Confidence reading technical drawings.

  • A willingness to work on the factory floor rather than next to it.

  • Problem-solving, initiative and ownership: you will often be the person who notices what others missed.

  • Manufacturing, quality or engineering experience, including from an internship or placement.

Nice to have

  • Metrology, inspection or QC experience.

  • Process improvement experience.

  • Exposure to precision manufacturing, aerospace, defence or energy.

Why Isembard

  • Learn quickly across engineering and manufacturing, with one-to-one mentorship.

  • Real room to advance as the quality function grows.

  • Competitive salary and equity.

Location: On-site at our Southwark factory in London.

title: Real Estate Transaction Lead, EMEA
descriptionHtml:
Mission

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

We are looking for a driven, transaction-focused real estate professional to own deal execution across the EMEA region. You will be part of a lean, high-velocity expansion team reporting directly to the Director of Real Estate. This is not a support role. You will run site selection, lead LOI negotiations, manage broker relationships, and drive leases to execution across a growing portfolio of healthcare retail clinics in your markets.

Neko is opening clinics at pace: the plan moves from a handful of sites today to a 2028 cohort in the dozens across EMEA and a global portfolio in the hundreds by 2030. Most in-house real estate roles at this scale sit inside large corporate structures where deals move slowly and decisions need layers of approval. Here, your deals matter immediately, your judgment is trusted, and the decisions you make in year one will shape the portfolio for the next decade.

The team is small and growing quickly, built around regional Transaction Leads covering the West, East, and Central United States and EMEA, supported by national specialists in market analysis, deal support, and lease administration. Many of these seats are still being filled, so you will help set the standard rather than inherit one.

What You’ll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Pipeline management: identify, evaluate, and advance sites across EMEA markets including the UK, Germany, the Nordics, and other major European cities. Markets are TBD and could extend across the region depending on demand.

  • Transaction execution: lead deals from initial market entry through signed lease, managing brokers, landlords, and timelines, at a pace set by the opening plan for the EMEA region.

  • LOI negotiation: draft, negotiate, and revise LOIs; own the deal process end to end from first tour to final execution.

  • Deal approval memos: build and present LOI and Lease Approval Memos with clear economics, risks, and a recommendation that stands up to executive scrutiny.

  • Landlord relationships: build and maintain relationships with institutional and private landlords across the EMEA region.

  • Broker coordination: manage tenant rep broker relationships across multiple markets simultaneously; hold brokers accountable to pipeline and timeline standards.

  • Cross-functional coordination: work closely with Legal, Construction, Design, and Facilities to move deals from signed lease into buildout.

  • Platform adoption: use Neko’s GIS site selection platform and lease administration system as the system of record and contribute to their rollout as the function scales.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 3 to 7 years of real estate transaction experience, with meaningful time spent in-house at a healthcare, wellness, or high-growth retail company.

  • You have personally led deals end to end, from site identification through LOI to signed lease, in competitive markets.

  • Comfort working in a startup environment with real pressure, fast timelines, and limited infrastructure. You build as you go.

  • A self-starter who does not need a fully defined playbook to do great work.

  • Strong communication skills. You can represent Neko professionally with institutional landlords while keeping internal stakeholders informed concisely.

  • Ability to read and pressure-test lease terms, rent schedules, and deal economics. You do not need to build financial models from scratch, but you need to know when a deal works and when it does not.

  • Familiarity with GIS tools and lease administration platforms is a plus; willingness to learn them quickly is a must.

  • AI: We use AI tools including Claude in daily work and expect you to use them too.

  • Based in Europe, within reasonable travel of the markets you cover. Experience working across multiple countries and lease regimes is a plus.
